correctness.rationale: The explicit complex polygon is orthogonal to constants and has every squared price-c and price-d edge chord proportional respectively to c and d, giving a global Rayleigh bound for every feasible allocation. The stated positive a,b meet the unit-price budget and their full two-vertex Bloch spectrum has Fiedler eigenvalue equal to the bound. At any alternative optimizer equality enforces the same complex vector eigenrelation, whose consecutive noncollinear circle chords force every real conductance perturbation zero, proving unique global optimality including the four-cycle. Trigonometric limits prove the asymptotic. The packaged checker verifies 2 exact rational identities, 75 spectra, 1350 dual chords and 600 asymmetric allocations; it is finite corroboration, not proof.

originality.rationale: Full-text comparison with Sun–Boyd–Xiao–Diaconis (2006), Section 5.3, identifies only the unit-cost explicit cycle optimum and a general-cost dual dimensional bound; this does not give the price-dependent closed form or edgewise uniqueness. Boyd–Diaconis–Parrilo–Xiao (2009) and Gerencsér–Hendrickx–Van Dooren (2015) address discrete-time criteria rather than the present continuous-time cost-normalized optimum. Exact-formula web queries and semantically broad mathematical-result lookups revealed no covering statement. Search incompleteness is a residual risk.
residual_risks: An equivalent specialized closed-form formula might exist in historical weighted-cycle or spring-ring optimization literature not retrieved; unsuccessful searches cannot rule that out.

A generic SDP framework computationally handles this case, but does not by itself state the exact closed-form classification and uniqueness; priority for specific consequences remains subject to broader historical discovery.

value.rationale: The high-impact original continuous-time fastest-mixing literature explicitly solved uniformly priced cycles while marking nonuniform-cost cycles as harder. Period-two prices form the canonical symmetry-preserving but nontrivial next step; this theorem simultaneously yields the unique optimizer over all asymmetric feasible conductances, an exact objective and constructive global dual polygon for every even size and positive cost ratio. Its square-root price response captures a non-obvious large-ring economic allocation law and replaces numerical SDP by elementary formulas.
